messages:
Emma: Quick sync — Atlas Retail asked for a performance bench for their cart-recommendation endpoint next week. They gave target: sustained ~1,000 qps, p99 < 120ms, typical inputs 64 tokens but 95th up to 512 tokens. Also flagged HSM + VPC peering on the security questionnaire. Can we assemble SRE + SE + solutions to coordinate test plan, cost, and security answers?

Liam: We can run this on Dedicated. My quick ask: confirm model variant, tokenization (are those input+output tokens?), and whether embeddings are part of the flow. Propose: warmup + steady-state runs, and a longer soak to validate KV cache behavior.

Sophia: SE here — flow includes an embed call for context lookups (~10% of requests). I'd recommend rdx-13b-q4 as a starting point. If Atlas needs higher quality, we can try rdx-70b but that changes capacity math.

Jordan: From runtime side: for 1k qps at 512 tokens (worst-case) we should assume ~6-8 x A100/80GB equivalents to hit p99 targets with caching. KMS/HSM for private deployments adds ~2–6ms per request if we sign per-request, but that's only in Private mode. I'll draft a concrete node plan and prewarm procedure.

Morgan: I'll own the security questionnaire bits (KMS/HSM, data-in-transit, data-at-rest, SOC2). For HSM attestation they want an external cert — need legal & infra review but we can provide a runbook and sample MCP. Also propose offering a short Dedicated trial with network isolation so they get demos of peering.

Emma: Awesome — can someone post an actual load command and a rough bench schedule? Atlas wants the plan to include ramp, steady-state, and post-run artifact delivery.

Liam: Example load commands we use for these tests: 
```
# vegeta (HTTP targets file)
vegeta attack -targets=atlas.targets.txt -rate=1000 -connections=300 -duration=5m | vegeta report -type='hist[0,50ms,100ms,200ms,500ms]'
```
Or k6 if they prefer JS scripting: `k6 run --vus 1000 --duration 5m script.js`

Jordan: Bench plan outline: 
- Prewarm: 5m warmup (steady ramp 0->1k qps)
- Steady-state: 3 runs of 5m each (collect token counts, KV cache hit ratio, CPU/GPU, PCIe metrics)
- Soak: optional 30m at 1k qps to validate degradation/GC
- Failure injection: short test routing to fallback model (rdx-7b) to verify graceful degradation
- Artifacts: raw logs, perf traces, per-token cost estimate, dashboard snapshots
I'll create the dedicated cluster reservation and config a canary fallback in the routing policy.

Morgan: High-level bench cost (rough estimate for sales SOW):
- Short bench (1–2 hours including prewarm + runs): $2k–5k (covers reserved GPUs + cloud infra + support)
- Extended soak (several hours): add $5k–15k depending on hours and model size
I will produce a precise per-hour burn after Jordan posts exact node counts.

Sophia: Security notes for questionnaire: 
- KMS: customer-managed key supported via KMS integrations (we provide guidance for key rotation).
- HSM: we can support HSM-backed signing for Private deployments; attestation requires a short legal/infra intake.
- Network: support VPC peering and private endpoints; can provide peering templates and runbook.
I'll drop a skeleton answers doc here once legal okays the wording.

Emma: Action items: 
- @Jordan: create dedicated bench cluster and post node counts (EOD tomorrow)
- @Liam: reserve load generators and run the tests Wed 10am PT (Atlas preferred)
- @Morgan: finalize security questionnaire answers and a bench cost range
- @Sophia: finalize prompt set and confirm model variant and embed ratio
Emma: I'll update SOW + send Atlas a proposed Wed 10am PT slot after we confirm nodes. :thumbsup:

Liam: Wed 10am PT works for me. I'll reserve nodes and upload the expected capacity numbers to the runbook.

ops-bot: benchmark-cluster-reservation #R-2026 created by Jordan (expires in 72h)

Jordan: Quick tip from past runs — cold-starts can spike p99 for ~20–45s. We should include a 5m prewarm and check KV cache priming. Also enabling continuous batching will help per-token throughput at the cost of a few ms latency in the steady tail.

Emma: Noted re: prewarm & KV priming. Morgan — can you confirm whether HSM attestation timeline (legal + infra) is ~2–3 weeks? Atlas needs that for procurement.

Morgan: Tentative timeline: legal intake + infra verification typically 7–14 business days. If they need SOC2 / cert copies faster we can provide existing certificates within 48h. HSM attestation itself depends on their vendor — I'll start the intake.

Sophia: I uploaded a sample small prompt set and a 1k-request synthetic generator (small corpus) to the shared folder: link https://redwood.internal/bench/atlas-requests — use that as `atlas.targets.txt`.

Liam: After the run I'll post a short results summary here. Plan to capture: p50/p95/p99, error rate, token/s, GPU utilization, and any spike patterns.

Emma: Thanks team. If we meet these timelines I can push a statement to Atlas that we can run the bench Wed and deliver artifacts + cost sheet within 48h of completion.

[Later, post-run - Liam]: Run complete (Wed 10:00 PT). Quick summary: 3 steady runs at 1k qps, rdx-13b-q4, inputs sampled from Sophia's set. Results snapshot: p50 24ms, p95 86ms, p99 132ms (just over the 120ms target). Error rate 0.12% (network retries), KV cache hit 38%. Switching to rdx-13b with aggressive cache priming reduced p99 to 118ms in a follow-up run. Full artifacts uploaded to runbook.

Jordan: Nice. Notes: the small delta was due to cache coldness and a tiny hotspot on one node (driver issue) — fixed by rebalancing. No infra blockers.

Morgan: I'll attach the proof points for encryption + HSM options and follow up with legal for attestation timeline.

Emma: Perfect — I'll update Atlas with the results and include the cost estimate for a one-time bench and options for Dedicated pilot. Thanks everyone :rocket:
